questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: First of all, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam had specific courses about Neurobiology which I was very interested in. Second, I always wanted to live in Amsterdam since I find the city very interesting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had an amazing experience. I was lucky with the university, the city and especially the people I met.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would say it was pretty easy. Check your mails and reach out to people if you are in doubt.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a very nice introduction-week where it was possible to ask all the questions one might have. Very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: VU is a very well-organized University. I found it easy to access the information I needed.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorms with shared or private facilities.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Cooking facilities involved shared kitchens for my behalf. I dont know about the other options

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is very fun and social! A good way to meet new people. It can also become pretty intense and exhausting, so it is important to take some time alone to charge (at least in my case).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was cheap, easy, fun and socail. Maybe not the best facilities, and unfortunately placed a little outside the city.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I found the courses on their website and applied through a guide I found there (along with a guide from KU). I would say that it was pretty intuitive.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I contacted some people through e-mail if I needed answers to my questions. I think it is also possible to call someone? In general, most information can be found on the websites of KU and the host university (VU)

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful - it was easy and I registered for the courses I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at the websites, don't feel too scared to ask for help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would say the academic level is pretty high. Maybe similar to KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was pretty different, which took me a while to get used to. There is way more group-work at VU, weekly assignments, and everything is more "scheduled" and mandatory. On the other hand, there was a bigger division between school-days and weekends, meaning that the weekends were mostly without any school-work on my behalf. In comparison, I think UCPH is based more on individual responsibility and planning (eg. catching up with lost work on the weekends)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I took the minor Brain and Mind with 5 courses of 6 ECTS points each

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think choosing courses is based mainly on interest of the student applying, and therefore I cannot recommend specific courses. I personally did though really enjoy the courses: Brain in Trouble and Developing Brain (each is 6 ETCS)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Hmm partying maybe. Also, if you go to Amsterdam you should really rent/buy a bike

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general living is cheaper, but not that much. Public transport is pretty expensive unfortunately - therefore I recommend getting a bike

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think there was many, although I didn't really apply to any. I mainly spend time in the city or with friends

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Biking around the city! Also - Amsterdam has a lot of nice museums and outdoor green areas (parks, the forest, etc). Cinemas and bars are very nice also. Good fleamarkets for shopping

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Museums (I loved Foam, Stedelijk, the Eye, Anne Frank), green areas; Amsterdam Bos, Vondelpark etc, second-hand shopping at Mevius or Waterlooplein Fleamarket, trying out food at Albert Cuypmarkt, idk - explore! And GET A BIKE

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I would say it was pretty easy. Amsterdam is not that different from Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I honestly didnt socialize with locals - all the friends I got was also foreigners on exchanges or similar. I think this is very common, and I personally don't care if my friends are from London or Serbia or The Netherlands... So maybe just accept that the chances of befriending dutch people are pretty low

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language a bit. But people are very good at english, fortunately. Also - they bike like crazy compared to Copenhagen, so be aware of that. Also, dutch food is not that interesting

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Amsterdam is beautiful. I love the bars and the museums, and I honestly loved everything about living there (but I also think that I was very lucky).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) be open, and try to socialize with new people even though they might not look as someone you would normally befriend. 2) get a bike and go exploring! 3) dont be to anxious about school and filling out official stuff and all that - everything always work out in the end, and you should really try to enjoy and have fun whilst being abroad

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask questions. Have some good rain-clothes. Dont plan too much - you'll have no idea how things end up anyways. And just GO!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met, without a doubt. I've gotten some very close friends from all around the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being on my own - especially in the beginning. It felt scary and overwhelming and uncomfortable. But as time passed, I met some really good people and everything fell into place.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Dont take it all to seriously - pick some interesting courses, follow them, but also enjoy life and have fun! I think going to Amsterdam will be a great experience, especially if you are open and not too afraid to talk to new people

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
